text:
Jakob Chychrun scored 26 goals last season, a rare number for a defenseman, and has 2 in 16 games this season. One of them, a power-play goal against Dallas, ended a drought; RMNB had more fun with the night he lost a skate blade and Alex Ovechkin pushed him along, hockey's version of the Tush Push.

The shooting is the whole story. He has 50 shots, more than three a game, and is shooting 4% against a usual range closer to 8%. His expected goals (3.1) say he's been a little unlucky on top of that. He's near the bottom of the league in wins added by goals.

Everything else is steady. He has 12 points, 6 on the power play, and 8 assists over his last ten games. Washington gets 53% of the expected goals at five on five with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd of 215 defensemen last season and better than his results, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his home-plate chances in the 92nd percentile among defensemen. Watch the shot count. With that volume, the goals don't stay away.
headline: Chychrun's shots aren't finding the net
